claims.content: More than half of Brazilians are overweight and have an associated comorbidity.
Around 20% of Brazilians are already in the obesity range.
Weight-loss medications are commonly known as weight-loss pens.
Liraglutide is a weight-loss medication approved in Brazil.
Liraglutide is sold under the brand name Saxenda.
Semaglutide is a weight-loss medication approved in Brazil.
Semaglutide is known as Wegovy.
Semaglutide is known as Ozempic.
Tirzepatide is a weight-loss medication approved in Brazil.
Tirzepatide is sold as Mounjaro.
When a person gains weight, their body attempts to maintain the weight they have gained.
When a person takes weight-loss medication, they feel less hungry and become full more quickly.
Obesity is a chronic disease, similar to diabetes or hypertension.
Obesity is a chronic disease that can be cured.
Obesity may not be cured, and a person may regain weight at any time.
The assessment of which weight-loss medication is most appropriate for a person's case must be individualized.
The assessment of which weight-loss medication is most appropriate for a person's case must be performed by a physician.
Weight-loss medications are sold only with a prescription to protect the patient's health.
Improper use of weight-loss medications without medical guidance can cause adverse effects.
People who seek weight-loss treatment on their own may experience unpleasant side effects.
People who seek weight-loss treatment on their own may experience drug interactions.
People who seek weight-loss treatment on their own may experience excessive loss of muscle mass known as sarcopenia.
People who seek weight-loss treatment on their own may experience hair loss.
People who seek weight-loss treatment on their own may experience brittle nails.
People who seek weight-loss treatment on their own may experience malnutrition.
People who seek weight-loss treatment on their own may experience pancreatic toxicity.
People who seek weight-loss treatment on their own may experience the risk of obtaining counterfeit medications.
The goal of weight-loss medications is not to help people lose a few pounds for aesthetic reasons.
The goal of weight-loss medications is to restore health and quality of life.
